title: Fallout Storm
bodyText: The sky turns a sickly amber. Fine ash begins to settle on everything outside. The Geiger counter screams.

title: Scavenger at the Door
bodyText: A gaunt figure stands at the bunker entrance, hands raised. They carry a pack and a worn-out rifle. They ask to trade.

title: Air Filter Failure
bodyText: A grinding noise from the ventilation shaft. The air filter has seized. Dust and faint radiation leak into the shelter.

title: Radio Transmission
bodyText: Through layers of static, a voice: coordinates, a supply cache, and a warning about what guards it.

title: Water Contamination
bodyText: The stored water tastes metallic. A quick check with the dosimeter confirms it: the supply is hot.

title: Sick Stranger
bodyText: A coughing figure stumbles into the airlock. Their skin is mottled with radiation burns. They collapse before speaking.

title: Generator Failure
bodyText: The lights flicker and die. The generator coughs once, then silence. Cold seeps in immediately.

title: Rats in the Stores
bodyText: Droppings in the food crate. Something has been gnawing at the ration packs. The scratching comes from the walls.

title: Shouting in the Dark
bodyText: Raised voices echo through the bunker. Two survivors are arguing over the last iodine pill. The tension is reaching a breaking point.

title: Supply Drop Rumor
bodyText: A crackling radio message mentions a military supply drop three miles north. Could be real. Could be a trap.

title: Hatch Seal Breach
bodyText: A high-pitched whistle from the outer hatch. The rubber gasket has cracked. Fallout-laced air seeps in.

title: Dry Pipes
bodyText: The water barrel is nearly empty. Rationing has begun, but thirst is already setting in. Desperation grows.

title: Heater Overheat
bodyText: The heater unit glows red-hot. A acrid smell fills the shelter. Someone needs to shut it down before it catches fire.

title: Dead Dog Outside
bodyText: A stray dog lies dead near the airlock, fur patchy, ribs showing. Fallout got it. A reminder of what waits outside.

title: Cabin Fever
bodyText: The walls feel closer every day. Someone hasn't spoken in three days. Another paces endlessly. The bunker was not built for this many people.

title: Old Diary
bodyText: Behind a loose panel, a diary from the bunker's original occupant. The last entry is dated three weeks after the bombs. It does not end well.

title: Ash Accumulation
bodyText: Radioactive ash has piled up against the air intake. If it's not cleared, the filters will clog within hours.

title: Medicine Trade
bodyText: A trader at the gate claims to have anti-rad medication. They want food in return. The deal feels too good.

title: Hidden Power Cell
bodyText: While clearing debris, a sealed power cell is found behind a wall panel. Still charged. Could power the radio for weeks.

title: Night Terrors
bodyText: Someone wakes screaming. They dreamed of the flash, the heat, the silence after. No one sleeps well anymore.

title: Filter Wear
bodyText: The air filter's indicator has dropped into the yellow. Replacement is needed soon, or the air quality will suffer.

title: Lucky Find
bodyText: A sealed crate in the corner, overlooked until now. Inside: canned food, a water filter, and a working flashlight.

title: Radiation Spike
bodyText: The dosimeter alarm triggers. Radiation levels inside the bunker have spiked. Something is leaking.

title: Old Music
bodyText: Someone finds a working music player with a single battered disc. For a few minutes, the bunker feels almost human again.

title: Wall Crack
bodyText: A hairline crack has appeared in the bunker wall. Water seeps through when it rains. If it widens, the shelter is compromised.

title: Dead Air
bodyText: The civilian broadcast cut out mid-sentence. No carrier, no static. Just a thin repeating tone, then silence. We tried every frequency. Nothing.

title: Trader in a Hurry
bodyText: The trader took the iodine without haggling. Didn't look at the food. Said they'd be back in two days, maybe less. Packed lighter than usual going out.

title: Numbers Station
bodyText: An automated military frequency cycling through cipher blocks. No operator, no preamble, just beeps at fixed intervals. Marcus sat and listened for an hour. Said it means nobody's left to talk.

title: Static, Then a Voice
bodyText: An international station cut in over the interference. The anchor's voice was shaking. 'Do not—' the signal collapsed. We never found out what not to do.

title: The Shelling Stopped
bodyText: Last night the artillery reached a fever pitch, shells falling close enough to feel in the floor. By morning, no gunfire at all. Just the wind against the hatch. Nobody slept through it.

title: A Knock in the Ash
bodyText: Three slow knocks on the outer hatch. Deliberate. Not debris, not wind. High fallout outside — the ash is coming down like grey snow. Whoever is out there cannot see, and neither can you.

choices.text: Open the hatch. Pull them in.
Say nothing. Step away from the hatch.

title: The Stranger Wakes
bodyText:
He opens his eyes on Day 37. Radiation burns across his neck. He was a cartographer. Says he knows a pre-war cache — sealed, untouched. Grid coordinates. He writes them down on a strip of packaging.

He needs water. He's barely holding on.

choices.text: Give him the clean water.
Give him the irradiated water. He won't know the difference.

title: The Scraping
bodyText: On Day 38, it starts again — but this time not knocking. A long, slow scraping against the outer hatch seal. Something methodical. Then silence for six hours. Then again. It continues for two days, then stops.

choices.text: You made your choice. Keep the hatch sealed.

title: The Coordinates
bodyText:
The address the stranger wrote. Grid reference for what he called a 'pristine pre-war cache'. Could be medicine, sealed food, batteries. Could be exactly what it says on the paper.

You have his word. And the memory of the water you gave him.

choices.text: Send someone to the coordinates.
Burn the paper. Don't risk it.

title: The Emissary
bodyText: Someone from the scavenger camp stands at the hatch. Hands empty, voice dry. They want water — enough for three, they say. The canteen at their hip is dented and light.
threateningBodyText: The same voice at the hatch, but the tone has changed. Not asking. They know what you have. The words are short: open up, or they come back with friends.

choices.text: Pass a jug of clean water through the hatch.
Keep the seal. Tell them we have nothing to spare.
Lie and say the purifier is broken.
Preemptively open fire through the hatch.

title: The Favor
bodyText: Two days later, the same voice at the hatch — softer. A half-crate of canned goods sits on the threshold. Payment for the water, they say. No weapons in sight.

choices.text: Take the crate. Nod once. Close the hatch.
Leave it. We don't take debts we can't see.
Search them for weapons before anything comes in.

title: The Mechanic
bodyText: They came back with a thin man who smells of solder. He listens at the hatch for the purifier's hum. The lie is thin now. They wait.

choices.text: Admit it. Pass a jug through and call it a misunderstanding.
Double down. Blame the filters. Blame the weather. Blame anything.
Offer to check their canteen filter — real help, no water lost.
Say nothing. Seal the hatch. Wait them out.

title: The Grudge
bodyText: Three days. Same hatch. Fewer words. They want water or they want a reason to stop asking politely.

choices.text: Pay up late. One jug, no apology.
Keep it sealed. Let the grudge sit.

title: After the Hatch
bodyText: No knock. Just bootprints in the ash leading away from the hatch, then a radio burst on the scavenger band that cuts off mid-word. Someone will come back heavier.

choices.text: Brace the hatch. Double the watch.
Leave it. Hope the ash covers the prints.

title: The Contaminated Water Trade
bodyText: A gaunt woman pounds on the hatch. Behind her, a child coughs — a wet, rattling sound. 'Please,' she begs. 'Clean water. Just enough for my daughter. I have ammunition. Military-grade. It's yours.' The bunker's water reserves are already low.

choices.text: Trade the water. A child's life is worth it.
We can't spare it. Every drop counts.
Half now. Half if she brings more ammunition.

title: The Infected Refugee
bodyText: A survivor stumbles into the airlock and collapses. Their skin is mottled — not radiation burns, but something else. A rash spreading up their neck. They're burning with fever. 'I just need to rest,' they whisper. 'Please don't send me back out.' The bunker has no quarantine room.

choices.text: Confine them to the stores room. Everyone stays clear.
Welcome them in. We don't abandon the sick.
Close the hatch. The risk is too great.

title: The Sabotaged Filter
bodyText: The air filtration unit failed overnight. But the filter isn't just worn — it's been cut. Someone inside the bunker deliberately damaged it. The cut is clean, deliberate. Paranoia spreads faster than radiation.

choices.text: Search every room. Question everyone.
Replace the filter. Say nothing. Watch from the shadows.
Call a meeting. Whoever did this, come forward. No punishment.

title: The Faction Deserter
bodyText: A Garrison officer in full uniform stands at the hatch, hands raised. 'I'm deserting,' they say flatly. 'I have schematics — patrol routes, supply caches, artillery positions. But the Garrison will come looking for me. They always do.' The officer waits for your answer.

choices.text: Welcome them in. The intel is worth the risk.
Give us the schematics and we'll give you supplies. Then go.
We can't afford a Garrison manhunt. Leave.

title: The Stranded Expedition
bodyText: The radio crackles: 'This is Scavenger Team Three — we're trapped. The building collapsed. Mika is pinned. The radiation is climbing. We need help. Please.' The coordinates are deep in a high-radiation zone. Sending a rescue team risks multiple lives to save one.

choices.text: Send a rescue team. No one gets left behind.
Guide them over the radio. Talk Mika through freeing herself.
We can't risk more lives. I'm sorry.

title: The Stolen Iodine
bodyText: The iodine pill count doesn't match. Ten pills missing. Marcus accuses Suki — 'She was in the stores alone yesterday.' Suki denies it, voice cracking. 'I would never. Someone is framing me.' Both are valuable. Both are furious. The pills are still missing.

choices.text: Search everyone's quarters. Find the truth.
Sit them down together. Work this out.
Both lose rations for a week. That's fair.

title: The Dying Trader's Bargain
bodyText: A trader collapses at the hatch, a locked military crate dragging behind them. Their skin is grey, eyes sunken. 'Terminal,' they rasp. 'Got maybe two days. This crate — it's worth more than you can imagine. Just let me die somewhere warm. Somewhere with walls.' The crate's lock is military-grade. No key in sight.

choices.text: Bring them inside. Make them comfortable.
Take the crate. They can die outside like everyone else.
We don't need a corpse in the bunker. Move on.

title: The Broken Generator
bodyText: The generator seizes at 3 AM. Temperature: -15°C outside. The remaining battery has one hour of charge. You can route it to the air filtration system — or to the room heaters. You cannot do both. In the dark, people start to shiver. In the silence, the filter stops humming.

choices.text: Route to heaters. We'll breathe unfiltered air but we won't freeze.
Route to filtration. The air stays clean — bundle up.
Split it. Half to each. Neither will be enough, but it's fair.

title: The Unwanted Bounty
bodyText: A warlord's messenger arrives at the hatch with a photograph. It's one of your survivors — wanted for 'crimes against the free market.' The bounty: three months of food. 'Just tell us where they are,' the messenger says. 'No one has to know it was you.' The accused survivor watches from the shadows.

choices.text: Tell the messenger to leave. Our people are not for sale.
The bounty is too low. Double it or walk.
Hand them over. Three months of food saves everyone else.

title: The False Distress Signal
bodyText: A repeating radio distress signal leads your scavenger team to a quiet building. Too quiet. The 'survivors' are mannequins. The 'supplies' are empty crates. The door slams shut behind them — tripwire. This was a raider ambush, carefully staged. Your team is trapped.

choices.text: Fight your way out. Use whatever cover you can find.
Offer a surrender. Trade half your gear for safe passage.
Radio for backup. Hold position until help arrives.
